names.display_en: The Deposed Emperor of Western Wei

summary: 文帝长子，三年无年号；谋除宇文泰事泄，废为安定公，旋遇害；其在位时西魏破江陵、灭梁元帝。
summary_en: Eldest son of Emperor Wen, he reigned three years without an era name; his plot against Yuwen Tai leaked, he was deposed as Duke of Anding and soon done to death; in his reign Western Wei broke Jiangling and destroyed Emperor Yuan of Liang.

portrait.appearance_basis: 史载无形貌描写。画像宜表现不甘受制的青年君主之态，衣冠从西魏制。属艺术想象。

timeline.title: 即位
timeline.summary: 文帝崩，钦即位（不建年号）。
timeline.summary_en: On Emperor Wen's death Qin took the throne — no era name was fixed.

timeline.title: 破江陵
timeline.summary: 西魏军破梁元帝于江陵。
timeline.summary_en: The Western Wei armies broke Emperor Yuan of Liang at Jiangling.

timeline.title: 被废
timeline.summary: 谋宇文泰事泄，废为安定公，立齐王廓。
timeline.summary_en: His plot against Yuwen Tai leaked; he was deposed as Duke of Anding and the Prince of Qi, Kuo, was set up.

timeline.title: 遇害
timeline.summary_en: He was done to death after the deposition.

timeline.title: 废帝总评
timeline.summary_en: He would have stood on his own, and failed.

relations.note: 大统十七年文帝崩，子钦即位

relations.note_en: Deposed in the third year; Yuwen Tai enthrones Kuo, Prince of Qi

bio_md:
# 西魏废帝 · 主要事迹

元钦，文帝长子。大统十七年文帝崩，钦即位——史称「不建年号」，其意在革除汉化之弊、复鲜卑旧制（宇文泰主导）。废帝在位三年，无所作为，国政尽归宇文泰：大统十七年，西魏军破江陵，灭梁元帝，「收其府库珍宝及宋齐梁之书」——南朝文化之精华，尽入关中。

废帝不甘傀儡，与宇文泰谋：「帝密谋诛泰，泰觉之。」三年，宇文泰废钦为安定公，立其弟齐王元廓，旋鸩杀钦，年三十。史评废帝：「欲自振而败。」西魏之皇权，自孝武西奔后已尽入宇文氏；元钦欲复皇权，然「时异势殊」，终以废死终。

西魏废帝之死，标志关陇集团「君权虚置」之定型：此后西魏恭帝、北周诸帝，皆宇文氏掌中之物。而破江陵一役，使西魏尽收南朝文物——隋唐制度之源，自西魏而盛。

> 参考：点校本《北史》卷005《魏本纪》、周书卷002《文帝纪》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yuan Qin, eldest son of Emperor Wen, took the throne on his father's death in the 17th year of Datong — the histories note he "fixed no era name," a move of Yuwen Tai's to strip away the sinicizing forms and restore Xianbei ways. Three years he reigned, doing nothing, the government wholly Tai's: in the 3rd year the Western Wei armies broke Jiangling and destroyed Emperor Yuan of Liang, "taking the treasures of his storehouses and the books of Song, Qi, and Liang" — the cultural wealth of the south passed into Guanzhong.

The Deposed Emperor would not be a puppet: "the emperor plotted secretly to slay Tai, and Tai learned of it." In the 3rd year Tai deposed Qin as Duke of Anding, set up his brother, the Prince of Qi, Kuo, and soon poisoned Qin, aged thirty. The histories say: "he would have stood on his own, and failed." Since Xiaowu's flight west, the power of the Western Wei throne was wholly the Yuwens'; Qin's attempt to restore it ended in deposition and death.

His fall fixed the "empty throne" of the Guanzhong bloc: from the Gong emperor of Western Wei through the emperors of Northern Zhou, the throne was the Yuwens' instrument. And the Jiangling conquest brought the south's books and institutions into Guanzhong — the sources of Sui–Tang institutions, gathered under Western Wei.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Beishi*, ch. 5 (Wei basic annals), and the *Zhoushu*, ch. 2 ("Annals of Emperor Wen").
